fretec.text: Fretec is a study in patience: matchup rating among the very best, bravery and resistance both at the very top, and a matchup kill-death line up near the top. The pace is measured, the headshot share thin, and the lifetime IvI down near the very bottom, yet the matchups sit at the top. The edge holds firm against the hardest third too, which is the mark of a player who saves their best for the hardest fights.

fatdobber.text: Fatdobber is a young account already fighting at the top: among the very best tracked across every count, with a furious tempo and the surest aim around. The output climbs with the opposition. The toughest-third hold stays high. Early read, but the first pages are hard to argue with.

friendlytester.text: Since 2014, FriendlyTester has been the definition of reliable: near the summit of everyone tracked, constant against any opposition. The hardest opposition never rattles them. The lifetime numbers line up with the matchups, which keeps the story clean. A veteran who shows up, holds the line, and makes every fight a little harder than expected.

funnycjack.text: FUNNYCJACK never lets the fight slow down: among the fastest killers in the game, in the upper reaches of everyone tracked, and unrelenting whatever the fight demands. The accuracy and headshots sit near the top too, which rounds out a complete card. A whirlwind who turns every exchange into a race the other side loses.

fantom220tr.text: Fantom220TR has been at this since 2015, and the years show as poise: top shelf on the whole ledger, with a trigger that runs warm and a game that sharpens as the bar rises. The aim is above average, the headshots land, and the lifetime numbers match the matchups. That is a strong regular, plain and simple.

fxgxgr.text: FXGXGR is the matchup board's quiet surprise: top shelf in the sampled fights, with resistance few can match and a kept share that stays firm as the stakes rise. The trigger runs at a good clip, yet the lifetime IvI reads middling and the aim is ordinary. The matchups hold the truer story here.

fireatomwall2.text: FireAtomWall2 has been around since 2018, and it shows: a steady output, staying power as the opposition improves, and a grade that sits top-shelf. The aim sits near the top, though the headshots are only middling. The lifetime IvI lands above average, a notch below the matchups.

friedicecream.text: FriedIcecream has been at this since 2018, and the years show: a top-shelf rating, with the most precise aim tracked and a high share of headshots. The work rate is relentless and the game keeps its shape as the enemies get tougher. Lifetime board backs up the matchups, end of story.

fussybaby.text: FussyBaby is a young account, big-game feel and all: a furious output, a game that never fades as the enemies get tougher, and a mark that sits top-shelf. Aim is precise, and headshots make up a high share of the shots. Early read, but the first pages already carry weight.

failswoop.text: Failswoop brings the complete package: top shelf in the matchups, swift, and solid as foes get stronger. The aim sits near the top, the headshots land close behind, and the pace always stays high. Career numbers and matchups line up neatly, no daylight between them.

fearandtrembling.text: fearandtrembling is the model of a complete game: top shelf in the matchups, brisk, and unfazed as foes get stronger. Aim is true with headshots close behind, and the tempo holds steady throughout. The career numbers match the matchups, which keeps the whole story straight.

faalswoop.text: Faalswoop hunts at full speed: the tempo is relentless, the courage holds against stronger enemies, the staying power holds, and the matchup kill-death mark sits near the top. The aim is sharp, headshots land above average, and the lifetime board puts the career near the summit. Consistency rests mid-pack — the only quiet line on a loud card.

feirmily.text: feirmily wins ugly and wins often: the adjusted rating heads the card, the tempo keeps coming, the staying power matches, and the matchup kill-death mark sits in the same tier. Accuracy sits below average, headshots land rarely, and the lifetime IvI sinks near the bottom — the lifetime board badly undersells this game. Consistency sags below average, but the results in real matchups speak plainly enough.

flarezest.text: Flarezest burns bright on every line: the adjusted rating runs high, the pace never drops, the nerve holds, the staying power stays firm. The matchup kill-death mark walks alongside. The output is relentless, the aim runs true, and headshots land with pleasing regularity. The lifetime board seconds that, rating the career among the top ranks, and consistency rests mid-pack.

foxyhahnderalkoholiker.text: FoxyHahnDerAlkoholiker plays at a sprint from first contact: a furious work rate, bravery that rises with the opposition, and accuracy near the top. The consistency mark slips below average, the single flaw in an otherwise relentless card, and the lifetime IvI lands above average. A whirlwind who rarely lets a fight cool down.

falcofr.text: FalcoFR is a young account with an old soul: tempo and bravery both in the upper tier, resistance right there. The matchup kill-death mark crowds the top. Accuracy runs top-shelf; the lifetime IvI already sits in the upper tier. Consistency sits below average, so the edge still has to prove itself against the strongest third — early days, but the first pages promise plenty.

fistenjoyer.text: FistEnjoyer keeps the engine running hot: the matchup rating rides near the top, the tempo matches it, and the game never wilts against tougher enemies, with a kill-death mark up there as well. The tempo runs above average, accuracy sits well above average. Lifetime numbers agree, sitting in the same strong range. A steady, high-volume presence with no quiet stretches.

foxycatortr.text: FoxycatorTR brings the noise: one of the busiest outputs tracked, a matchup rating near the top, with a game that climbs as enemies improve close behind. Matchup kill-death sits there too, and the lifetime board runs a step below the matchups. Headshots run middle of the road, which only makes the volume more impressive.
